assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction in electron optics is a genuine invention that opened a door: sub-angstrom, atom-by-atom imaging and spectroscopy of interfaces, defects and nanostructures across materials physics, chemistry and nanoscience. It overcame Scherzer's long-standing theorem limitation and is now routine in laboratories worldwide. As a practising microscopist I can attest to its practical impact, though that closeness also calls for caution about my own bias.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theoretical design of the corrector concept, Haider led the realisation of the hexapole corrector for TEM, and Urban led the application to atomic-resolution materials imaging. These three are the natural configuration. Other contributors (e.g. the STEM corrector work of Krivanek and colleagues) are not in the supplied credit and their relative priority needs checking in the historical record.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally demonstrated in the late 1990s and independently confirmed by many groups and commercial instruments over two decades. Interpretation is stable and recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Priority relative to the parallel STEM aberration-corrector development is outside the supplied credit and unresolved.
Whether the committee regards an instrument of this kind as sufficiently physics rather than engineering; I rely on recollection of the history, not independent verification.
Some of my judgement may reflect my own field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, enables clocks with fractional uncertainty near 1e-18, opening tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. This is a clear invention with experimental verification and a strong 'new tool opens a door' character.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and realised the first strontium lattice clocks; Ye brought the clocks to record precision and stability. A two-person split is clean, though Ye's work also builds on frequency-comb advances already recognised in 2005 and on others' optical clock work (e.g. ion clocks) that are outside this entry.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent laboratories confirm the performance and international comparisons are established. Timely, with redefinition of the second still pending.
uncertainties: Relation to prior prizes on laser spectroscopy, frequency combs and ion traps may make the committee view it as incremental.
Other groups (e.g. Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow) not credited here; fairness of a two-name configuration is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 confirmed the origin-of-mass mechanism and is one of the most decisive experimental results in particle physics. It is the original observation of the particle and has been verified by combined measurements at the LHC.
assessment.attribution: The prize for the mechanism already went to theorists in 2013, leaving the experimental side. The collaborations number thousands, so the fair configuration is genuinely hard; the founding proposers and leaders of ATLAS and CMS (Jenni, Della Negra, Virdee) are the most defensible three from the supplied names, though Gianotti led ATLAS at the time of the announcement and is an equally serious claimant. I do not claim to resolve this.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: independently confirmed by two experiments and by Run 2 and Run 3 coupling measurements. Recognition is overdue in timing terms.
uncertainties: Allocation among spokespersons, founders and the many physicists who drove the analyses is contentious.
The Nobel statutes limit to three, which leaves out one of four supplied names and the broader collaboration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube observation of a diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux in 2013 and the identification of a blazar (TXS 0506+056) and the Galactic plane as sources opened neutrino astronomy. This is a new observational window achieved through a major instrumentation effort.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube; Spiering is a long-standing leader of the neutrino telescope programme and Karle a senior leader in construction and analysis. Alternatives within the larger collaboration, and earlier pioneers of neutrino telescopes (e.g. DUMAND, Baikal, AMANDA) could challenge priority; I cannot settle that from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Diffuse flux confirmed by several channels; source identification is more recent and still being strengthened. Reasonably mature but partly young.
uncertainties: Evidence for individual sources is statistically modest compared with the diffuse flux.
Credit relative to ANTARES, Baikal and AMANDA pioneers is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators, with the experimental quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe and the quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetic topological insulator films, introduced a new class of materials with protected edge states, relevant to metrology and quantum devices. Both predictions were verified by decisive experiments.
assessment.attribution: Kane contributed key theory (with Mele) and Molenkamp's group made the original experimental observation of the QSH state, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and König et al. Xue's group made the first QAH observation. Credit is spread across theorists (Bernevig, Zhang, Mele, Fu) not in this list, and a compound discovery may need different recognition for different parts. Because I weigh the original experiment, I prefer Molenkamp and Xue, with Kane for the theory.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in multiple laboratories, though applications remain developing. Interpretation is stable.
uncertainties: Theory credit among Kane, Mele, Bernevig, Zhang and others is disputed and the supplied names omit some.
Two experimental discoveries bundled together may be a poor fit for one prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy spins in diamond created a room-temperature solid-state quantum system used in nanoscale magnetic and thermal sensing, including in cells, and in quantum registers. Experimental results are clear and widely replicated.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko made the first optical detection and coherent manipulation of single NV centres; Lukin's group extended this to quantum registers and sensing. The strongest original-experiment claim is Wrachtrup and Jelezko; Lukin's role is broader and overlaps with other candidates, so inclusion is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated by many groups; applications to sensing continue to mature. Timely.
uncertainties: Gruber et al. 1997 (single NV detection) and the Jelezko-Wrachtrup priority question are not detailed in the supplied credit.
Applications still maturing, so impact may not yet be fully demonstrated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-halide perovskite solar cells reached over 25% efficiency within a decade, a striking materials advance with real implications for energy. Physical understanding of defect tolerance and ion migration is still developing.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell in 2009, Park and colleagues the first solid-state devices with greater stability and efficiency in 2012, and Snaith's group the meso-superstructured cell. The three are a plausible set, though others (e.g. Grätzel, Kanatzidis) have arguable claims.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely, but long-term stability and toxicity remain open, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Device stability and lead content are unresolved.
Credit with Grätzel and others is disputed and not in the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2018 observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene created a new field of moiré quantum matter, built on the Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction of flat bands.
assessment.attribution: Jarillo-Herrero's group made the original experimental discovery (with Yuan Cao as first author, a junior researcher who cannot be included here); Bistritzer and MacDonald gave the theoretical prediction. The experimental discovery is the part I weigh most.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely in many laboratories, but still young; the mechanism of superconductivity is unresolved, which argues for waiting.
uncertainties: Recognition may be premature relative to the other candidates.
Credit to the early-career first author and other theorists is outside the supplied names.
